temperature.title: Why oxalate must be removed
temperature.description: Organic matter in bauxite degrades in the hot caustic liquor to sodium oxalate. If it builds up, oxalate co-precipitates with gibbsite, giving fine, weak hydrate and lower yield. A side-stream is cooled and seeded with oxalate crystals so oxalate crystallises in a controlled way; crystals are separated (cyclones/filters) and destroyed (e.g. by lime or burning), and the clean liquor returns.

foundation: Ring-wall or slab foundation designed for full liquid/slurry weight plus agitator dynamic loads; settlement monitoring for large tanks.
alignment: Tank plumb and level; agitator shaft vertical and concentric; check gearbox mounting.
piping: Nozzles sized for slurry velocity (avoid settling and erosion); flush connections; scaling-resistant design and descaling access.
Caustic service: suitable materials, gaskets and spray shields; eyewash/safety showers nearby.
commissioning: Water trials (agitator run with water, check vibration and power); then caustic/slurry; verify levels, interlocks and spillage containment (bunds).

lubrication: Agitator gearbox oil and motor bearings per maker; no lubrication for static parts.

video_tutorials.title: Oxalate Removal System — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Oxalate Removal System.
An oxalate removal system takes a side-stream of liquor, cools and seeds it so sodium oxalate crystallises in a controlled way, and separates the crystals in hydrocyclones or filters.
Clean liquor returns; part of the crystals is recycled as seed.
Typical applications include liquor purification in Bayer refineries; controlling organic impurities to protect hydrate quality.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Oxalate Crystallizer: Agitator Shaft & Impeller, Cyclone Feed Pump, Cyclone Feed Pump — Shaft & Coupling (turning).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Oxalate Removal System works.
Side-stream liquor enters the crystallizer.
Cooling jacket lowers temperature.
Oxalate grows on seed crystals.
The hydrocyclone separates crystals.
Seed is recycled.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Organic matter in bauxite degrades in the hot caustic liquor to sodium oxalate.

video_tutorials.title: Oxalate Removal System — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Oxalate Removal System.
Monitor oxalate in liquor.
Clean jacket/cyclone.
Cyclone liner replacement.
Watch for oxalate breakthrough: fine hydrate in precipitation. Common cause: poor removal.
Watch for jacket scaling: poor cooling. Common cause: scale.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
